topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets out the specific learning objectives.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and evolutionary origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how somatic mutations, endogenous cellular processes, and inherited genetic predispositions interact with the tissue microenvironment to drive cancer evolution.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens, risk perception, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between environmental exposures, public understanding of cancer causation, and geographic variations in cancer rates.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms by which pathogens drive malignancy, illustrated by the multifactorial pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and dietary or chemical mutagens undergo xenobiotic activation to form DNA adducts and induce mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, cellular susceptibility, and cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental susceptibility facilitate the clonal outgrowth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers closing remarks summarizing the lecture's core themes and framing carcinogen exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions.
